SnowDistribution: Icy paths and hillsides with isolated areas of deeper snow making progress slow.  Blizzard and whiteout conditions presenting challenging and serious conditions. Winds 30-40 mph, progress difficult and tiring.
Comment: Some uncertainty over forecast wind speeds with potential to be 10-20 mph stronger. Careful consideration required for runout zones in avalanche terrain.
WeatherInfluences:
Gale force South-South-East winds will decrease only slightly overnight, continuing  very strong throughout the period. 
Heavy snowfall overnight will ease to become patchy and light during the day. A complex freezing level with summit temperatures on average around -3.5 Celsius.
SnowStability: Fresh deposits of unstable windslab will develop overnight and through the day, primarily on North-West to North aspects above 1000 metres. West and North- East aspects will also be affected due to cross loading. The greatest instability will be in steep locations such as gullies, gully tops, coire rims and convexities. On these aspects, fragile cornices will develop. The avalanche hazard will be Considerable.
ObservedWeatherInfluences: Gale force South-South-East winds. Snow showers during the morning eased to become mostly dry during the afternoon. Snow initially falling to lower elevations, then became confined to above around 750 metres. The freezing level was 1000 metres.
ObservedSnowStability: Unstable windslab is lying on West through North to North-East aspects above 1000 metres. The greatest instabilities are in steep locations such as gullies, gully exits, coire rims and convexities. On these aspects, fragile cornices are present. The avalanche hazard is Moderate.
